<action type="say">
Got it—Lone Star Federal Platinum Rewards Visa. Here’s a focused game plan you can follow word‑for‑word.

1) How to reach them
- On the bank’s website: look for “Lost or Stolen Card” or “Report a Card Problem” under “Credit Cards” or “Customer Service.”
- In the mobile app/online banking: under “Cards” or your Platinum Rewards Visa, there’s often a “Report card lost/stolen” option that will also show you the correct phone number.
- If you still have a paper statement, the lost/stolen number is usually on the front or back.

2) Call script (you can read this)
“Hi, I’m calling to report my Lone Star Federal Platinum Rewards Visa as lost.  
I need you to:
1) Immediately block this card so no new charges can go through, and  
2) Issue me a replacement card as soon as possible.

I don’t have the card number handy, but I can verify my identity and any details on the account.”

When they’ve found your account, say:
“Please review my recent transactions with me. I want to check for anything unfamiliar or potentially fraudulent, especially in the last 30–60 days.”

3) Key questions to ask them
- Card security:
  - “Can you confirm the card is fully blocked and cannot be used anymore?”
  - “If you see any suspect transactions, are you opening a fraud claim or dispute for those today?”

- Replacement card:
  - “Will my replacement Platinum Rewards Visa have a new card number, expiration date, and CVV?”  
  - “When will it be shipped, and how long will it take to arrive?”  
  - “Will it be sent to [confirm your current mailing address]?”  
  - “Is there any fee for the replacement?”

- Autopay & online accounts:
  - “Will my existing autopay from my bank account still work, or do I need to re‑set it once I get the new card?”  
  - “Will my online banking login stay the same, and will the new card automatically show up there?”

4) After the call (your checklist)
- Log into online/mobile banking:
  - Confirm the old card shows as blocked or “lost/stolen.”
  - Check transactions over the last 30–60 days and note any you don’t recognize (time, amount, merchant).
- When the new card arrives:
  - Activate it immediately.
  - Update card details anywhere it’s saved (streaming services, phone bill, utilities, subscriptions, digital wallets like Apple/Google Pay).

If, when you’re reviewing your history, you see a charge that looks wrong, tell me the rough date, amount, and merchant (no personal info), and I’ll help you phrase exactly how to describe it as a dispute/fraud on the call or in secure messaging.</action>
